rules.mode_rule: known_at and reconstruction availability give identical results with original known_at; batch and full replay only; update, restore and merge unsupported (UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY)

knowledge_readiness.K: K is the knowledge cutoff (the instant up to which facts may be known). It is distinct from the market cutoff C (the instant up to which bars and endpoints may have completed); K may be later than C. A bar or fact is KNOWN iff its original known_at_ns is non-null and <= K (== K is known).
knowledge_readiness.enforcement: The shared AvailabilitySpec.knowledge_reason returns None in reconstruction mode, so a shared validator never excludes a late row in that mode. The producer therefore enforces knowledge itself, identically in known_at and reconstruction modes, from the original known_at_ns of every consumed row or fact: null is unknown_availability, > K is future_knowledge. No result depends on the mode.
knowledge_readiness.compact: In fixtures the compact token ka maps to known_at_ns = K_ns - (100 - ka) seconds with K_ns = C_ns + 100 s, so ka 100 is exactly K, 150 is 50 s after it and 50 is 50 s before it.

refusal_precedence.rule: A refusal raises the code of the first stage, in this order, that has a fault; a later stage is not evaluated for a row that failed an earlier one (so a row rejected by the shared validator is not also reported as a grid mismatch). Every refusal fixture is a single-fault recipe: exactly one defect, in the stage recorded in `stage`, and no other check fires on the mutated input (an independent reviewer audit collects every trigger, not only the first). A row that carries two defects is not a refusal fixture.
